title: Adaptive slot pooling and deferred coalescence for paged KV cache
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: In our paged attention KV cache, allocation churn and fragmentation during high-concurrency prefill bursts cause tail-latency regressions and unnecessary kernel switches. Small allocations plus eager compaction create CPU/GPU stalls; aggressive eviction policies cause decode stalls when long-lived context is re-requested. This ticket proposes an adaptive slot-pooling layer combined with deferred coalescence (compact-on-idle) and a prefill-aware admission policy to reduce fragmentation, limit kernel migration, and amortize compaction costs.
motivation: Customers running high-concurrency chat workloads (short prompts with occasional long context injections) see increased p99 latency when the runtime switches kernels mid-decode or when prefill queues trigger synchronous compaction. We need a strategy that reduces rework and keeps hot slices resident without sacrificing memory efficiency for large tenants.
proposal: 1) Introduce a thin slot-pool allocator that serves fixed-size slot bins (power-of-two and hybrid small/large bins) to reduce per-allocation meta overhead and minimize fragmentation.
proposal_more: 2) Implement deferred coalescence: instead of immediate cross-page compaction on eviction, mark pages as 'stale' and schedule compaction to run opportunistically during low GPU utilization or explicit maintenance windows. Compact-on-idle will use a bounded budget to avoid impacting SLOs.
proposal_kernel_routing: 3) Add kernel-stability hints to the allocator metadata so the kernel selector favors co-located allocations for sequential decodes, reducing kernel handoffs when prefill spans multiple pages.
prefill_policy: 4) Prefill admission: prefill requests are classified by predicted reuse score (based on recent touch frequency and token-span heuristics). Low-reuse prefill is demoted to ephemeral bins that are reclaimed aggressively; high-reuse prefill is pinned into a hot-residency ring with TTL and soft-protection from eviction.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: lowers fragmentation, reduces mid-decode kernel switches, amortizes compaction cost, improves p99 in mixed workloads.
- Cons: slightly higher memory overhead for reserved slot pools, complexity in allocator invariants and maintenance scheduling, potential delayed reclamation causing transient memory pressure if coalescer misses windows.
acceptance_criteria: p99 generation latency improvement >= 15% for mixed short+long chat synthetic workload compared to baseline (runtime-1.22)
compaction-induced GPU stalls reduced (compaction CPU time outside of critical path increased, in-path compaction decreased by 90%)
kernel switch-rate per-decode reduced by >= 30% under bursty prefill traffic
no regressions on max-resident-memory for 95th percentile tenants (>95% of tenants should have <= 5% extra memory overhead)
e2e rollout plan validated with canary traffic and automatic fallback to baseline allocator
implementation_plan: Spike (2d): prototype slot-pool allocator and simple hot-residency ring in a local runtime build; measure allocation latency and fragmentation snapshot
Design review (1d): circulate design doc and cost/benefit analysis; include runtime and console implications (metrics to surface)
Phase 1 (1w): implement slot-pool allocator with ephemeral and hot bins, add metrics: slot-utilization, fragment-count, kernel-switch-rate
Phase 2 (1w): implement deferred coalescer as background worker with configurable budget and idle-detection hook
Phase 3 (3d): integrate kernel-stability hints into kernel selector and add routing tests
Benchmarks (3d): run mixed workload harness (short chat + occasional long prefill) across instance types and quantify p50/p95/p99
Canary (3d): rollout to 5% traffic with runtime flag and monitoring dashboards; validate automatic rollback on SLO breaches
Post-mortem and docs (2d): update ops runbook, console alerting, and write RFC summarizing results
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator invariants, fuzz tests for eviction sequences, synthetic bench harness reproducing bursty prefill, integration tests exercising kernel-stability across model variants. Add a fault-injection test to simulate missed compaction windows and observe bounded memory pressure handling.
metrics_to_track: slot_alloc_latency_ms, slot_reuse_rate, page_fragmentation_ratio, kernel_switches_per_decode, compaction_worker_cpu_ms, p50/p95/p99_generation_latency, memory_residency_by_tenant
risks:
- Deferred coalescence could lead to transient OOM if idle windows are rare for busy clusters.
- Kernel-stability hints may interact poorly with heterogenous kernel placements across hardware generations.
- Complexity increases touch-surface for bugs in eviction logic.
mitigations:
- Add hard cap safeguards and an emergency sync-compact path triggered by resident-memory thresholds.
- Validate kernel hints with a hardware matrix during canary.
- Start with feature-flagged rollout and high-visibility dashboarding.
